newsitem.title: USA: Late NYMEX natgas still mixed, fronts up on cash.
newsitem.headline: Late NYMEX natgas still mixed, fronts up on cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained mixed late Friday in sluggish activity, with front months still holding gains amid reports of steady to slightly firmer weekend physical prices, market sources said.

At 1355 EDT, September climbed two cents to $2.197 per million British thermal units, while October was 1.4 cents higher at $2.19. Others remained mixed, with some 1998 and 1999 contracts still down slightly.

"The cash was perky in the face of some milder weather early next week, but we're still in a range until further notice," said one New York-based trader, noting conflicting forecasts for the end of the week.

Despite a brief weekend warmup in the Midwest and East, forecasters are calling for mostly seasonal to below-seasonal weather early next week. But end-week forecasts vary, with at least one expecting another bout of heat in the East, traders said.
Technical traders said the market was probably a bit overbought after recent gains and due for a pullback.

Most agreed September needed a close above $2.20 to turn sentiment more bullish. In the meantime, recent ranges were intact, with next resistance seen at the $2.27 double top. Near-supprt was pegged in the $2.15-2.16 area and then along the short-term up trendline in the $2.11 area. More important support was expected at $2.08 and then at last week's low of $2.045.

In the cash Friday, Gulf Coast weekend gas was steady to up slightly at about $2.20. Midcon pipes showed similar movement to the mid-teens. New York city gate weekend gas was up slightly to the mid-$2.40s.
NYMEX said 8,224 contracts traded at 1320 EDT.
On the KCBT, September was still up by one-half cent at $2.07, while deferreds remained steady to 1.5 cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 1.5 cents to 12.7 cents (NYMEX premium).
